analysis.subject: civics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers how poverty status is set using money income thresholds that vary by family size, do not vary geographically, are updated for inflation, with rules for counting income, excluded populations, and a worked family example showing ratio and surplus.

overview.headline: Poverty status set by comparing family income to thresholds

keyPoints.point: A family and everyone in it is considered to be in poverty when income is less than its threshold.
keyPoints.quote: Is less than the poverty threshold for that family - that family and everyone in it is considered to be in poverty.

keyPoints.point: Each person or family is assigned one of 48 possible poverty thresholds.
keyPoints.quote: The Census Bureau assigns each person or family one out of 48 possible poverty thresholds.

keyPoints.point: The same thresholds are used throughout the United States and do not vary geographically.
keyPoints.quote: The same thresholds are used throughout the United States (they do not vary geographically).

keyPoints.point: Poverty status uses before-tax money income and excludes capital gains and noncash benefits.
keyPoints.quote: money income before taxes and does not include capital gains or noncash benefits

keyPoints.point: Poverty status cannot be determined for people in institutional group quarters, college dormitories, and military barracks.
keyPoints.quote: Poverty status cannot be determined for people in:

keyPoints.point: Family income is compared to its threshold to calculate the ratio of income to poverty.
keyPoints.quote: The total family income divided by the poverty threshold is called the Ratio of Income to Poverty.

keyTerms.gloss: dollar amounts used to determine poverty status for families of different sizes
keyTerms.quote: Poverty thresholds are the dollar amounts used to determine poverty status.

keyTerms.gloss: before-tax cash income counted to compute poverty status
keyTerms.quote: money income before taxes and does not include capital gains or noncash benefits

keyTerms.gloss: inflation index used to update thresholds annually for price changes
keyTerms.quote: Thresholds are updated annually for inflation using the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U).

keyTerms.gloss: number found by dividing family income by its poverty threshold
keyTerms.quote: The total family income divided by the poverty threshold is called the Ratio of Income to Poverty.

keyTerms.gloss: dollar gap showing how far income falls below a familys poverty threshold
keyTerms.quote: is called the Income Deficit (for families in poverty)

keyTerms.gloss: set of people whose poverty status can be determined and included in totals
keyTerms.quote: they are excluded from the “poverty universe” (table totals).
